correctness.rationale: PASS: The superior state solves x=K/(1+q e^-rt), and the inferior growth rate a(t)=lambda+delta(t) strictly decreases, with delta=d e^-rt/(1+q e^-rt). The exact reciprocal z=1/y solves a linear equation and yields z-C/lambda=e^-F(1/y0-C/lambda-(C/lambda)I(t)), I=integral(delta e^F). Its improper integral is finite iff r>lambda, giving the explicit ycrit=lambda/[C(1+Iinf)]. The moving nullcline h=a/C decreases, and at each crossing y=h one has (y-h)'=-h'>0; hence at most one strict peak. The reciprocal sign forces existence precisely for ycrit<y0<h(0) if r>lambda and for all 0<y0<h(0) if r<=lambda. The exact equation L(y0)=G(t_peak) has G'=C e^F delta'/a²<0. Asymptotics of its two terms give A0=C zeta d r/[lambda²(r-lambda)] and thus logarithmic delay and power-law peak height. In independent checks the displayed example reproduces ycrit=1/(40+12pi), phase signs, and near-critical delay; numerical quadrature truncation is not an analytic proof. Boundary y0=ycrit increases without peak; y0=h(0) has zero initial slope and decreases afterwards.
